newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's Socialists, allies approve Dobrev as PM.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's Socialists, allies approve Dobrev as PM.

text.p: Coalition allies of Bulgaria's ruling Socialists on Wednesday approved Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev as prime minister to replace Zhan Videnov who resigned last month, a party spokeswoman said.
Dobrev, who was nominated by the Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) on Tuesday, immediately vowed to push ahead with economic reform.

"I will be ready to discuss with all political forces the problems of the economy and social order," Dobrev told a news conference. "I plan to carry out radical economic reforms which will boost economic growth."
President Zhelyu Zhelev is expected to give him a mandate to form a new cabinet on Friday and ask parliament within seven days to approve his nomination and vote on the new cabinet.
Videnov resigned at a party congress on December 21, after months of criticism of his handling of the economy, sparking a showdown between party hardliners and reformists.

Dobrev, 49, emerged as an outspoken critic of Videnov at the congress, attacking the cabinet's record in handling Bulgaria's economic and social crisis and raising the previously taboo issue of government corruption.
The BSP is expected to discuss a new cabinet on Sunday.
"Some of the ministers in the current cabinet will probably retain their posts in the new cabinet," said BSP official Lyubomir Kolarov.
A mining engineer by training, Dobrev was a leader of the Communist youth organisation Komsomol before 1989. He has also chaired parliament's national security committee.
Critics of his candidature say he lacks the economic background necessary to win the approval of Bulgaria's foreign partners.

The opposition Union of Democratic Forces says the Socialists do not have enough public support to form a new government and is stepping up street protests to call for early parliamentary elections instead.

"It is clear that by electing the interior minister to head the government, the BSP seeks to solve the problems of the street and not the problems of the country," UDF leader Ivan Kostov told reporters.
